threads.thread_goal: Align on scope, touchpoints, and overall pilot plan.

messages.text: Kicking off the Cross-Channel Customer Feedback Improvement Pilot for the next 30 days. Goal is to design and run a focused pilot that captures, routes, and acts on feedback across our main channels, then summarise results in a short roadmap. I will own the overall coordination and reporting. To get started, I have a draft list of touchpoints for T1 and a rough outline for the process map in A1. Proposal for scope: digital (website forms, email, social), ICT help desk tickets, membership interactions, insurance complaints, and cellar visits. For timing, we would run the pilot for 30 calendar days, with weekly KPI snapshots and a final evaluation aligned with T11. Before I lock this in, can each of you confirm which touchpoints you can realistically include, given the constraints on tools, privacy, and cellar operations?

From the ICT help desk side I can bring in all tickets where customers contact us via phone or email, plus any chat if it goes through our current system. For T1, I can help list and describe those touchpoints and how they are logged today. One concern is data privacy when we consolidate feedback from tickets with other channels, but that should be covered once we work through T9 and A7. For the 30-day window, I do not see a blocker as long as we keep using existing tools and a simple tagging approach. Do we want to include internal-only tickets, or limit to customer-facing ones for this pilot?

From membership, I can include email and phone interactions with members, and I can also add a short question at the end of our regular calls as part of T4. For T8 and T10 I will need some guidance on wording and training, but I can draft something simple. For the pilot scope, should we also count feedback that comes in via our newsletter replies, or is that better handled under digital channels?

On the insurance side, I suggest we include all formal complaints plus any written feedback that comes with claim documents. That will align well with T7 later when we map our existing complaint codes to the new taxonomy in A2. For T1, I can provide a list of our current intake points: email, postal mail, and the online claim form. The 30-day pilot is feasible for us, but we should be clear that we are not changing contractual terms, only how we classify and respond. I can help document that in A1 so stakeholders see the boundary.

From the cellar, I can include feedback from guided tours and tastings, using the checklist we will define in T6 and A3. Because of peak hours, I would limit collection to the end of each tour and not during active production. I can also pass any ad hoc comments visitors make about safety or product quality, but I will need a simple way to hand those to you, maybe via A5 or a quick form. For the 30 days, I can commit to using the checklist on all scheduled tours, as long as we keep it short.

On the question about internal-only tickets: for this pilot I suggest we focus on customer-facing tickets only, so that T11 and later T12 stay manageable. We can flag internal issues separately if they affect the feedback flow, but not treat them as pilot feedback items. I will reflect that in the T1 mapping and A1 process map. If anyone sees a strong reason to include internal tickets, please speak up now.

Focusing on customer-facing tickets works for me. I will still note any internal tickets that highlight routing or privacy issues so we can feed them into T9 and the risk log, but they will not be counted as feedback volume in A6. I will start pulling a list of the main customer ticket types today for T1.

On newsletter replies: I suggest we treat them as in scope but route them through the digital bucket in T1, with membership flagged as a stakeholder when the feedback is clearly about member benefits or communication. That way we do not miss useful input, but we also do not overload your team with manual logging. I will add a line in A1 to show that path and make sure A5 has a field to mark origin as newsletter.

Treating newsletter replies as digital but flagging membership sounds good. I can help tag a sample of those during the pilot so we see how often they come up. For T4, I will keep the member interaction questions short so they fit naturally into calls and emails.

Agree on clarifying that we are not changing coverage. When we document the insurance touchpoints in T1, I will add a short note for each channel about what customers can expect, so that later A4 and T3, T4 scripts stay consistent. For the pilot timeline, I would prefer we align the start date with the beginning of a claims reporting week, so we do not split our internal reporting periods. Is there flexibility on the exact start day within the 30-day window?

On the cellar side, I will need a bit of help to make sure the checklist in T6 lines up with the taxonomy in A2, so that what we capture on paper can be tagged correctly in A5. Also, for operational impact, I suggest we avoid collecting feedback during harvest days in the busiest hours. Maybe we can define specific time windows in A1 so staff know when to use the checklist.

We do have flexibility on the exact start date as long as we still complete T11 and T12 within the 30-day overall deadline. Proposal: start the pilot next Monday, run for 30 days, with weekly async KPI snapshots and a short end-of-pilot retrospective feeding into A8. That should align with your claims reporting cycle and give us four full weeks of data. If no one objects by tomorrow, I will treat that as our agreed timeline.
Next Monday start works for the help desk. I will be ready with the T1 touchpoint list and a first pass at the intake script for T3 so we can test it early in the pilot.
The proposed start date is fine for membership. I will use this week to sketch the member question set for T4 and a first draft of the customer-facing message for T8, then share for feedback.
Starting next Monday works well for insurance. I will prepare the list of complaint touchpoints for T1 and identify a small batch of historical complaints we can reclassify later under T7 as a test.
Next Monday is fine for the cellar. I will adjust tour briefings so we can add the checklist from T6 at the end without slowing down operations too much.

Good point on harvest days. In A1 I will specify that cellar feedback via A3 is collected at the end of tours and not during peak production windows, and we will reflect that in the pilot constraints. That should keep T6 practical while still giving us enough data for T11.

Summarising where we landed so far: in scope for the pilot are digital channels including website forms, email, social, and newsletter replies; ICT help desk customer-facing tickets; membership calls and emails with a short feedback question; insurance complaints and written feedback; and cellar tours using the checklist. Internal-only tickets are out of scope for volume but can inform improvements. We will start next Monday and run for 30 days, with weekly KPI snapshots and a final evaluation feeding into A8. I will update A1 and T1 to reflect this and treat this as our confirmed scope and timeline for the pilot.

threads.thread_goal: Define and finalise the unified feedback taxonomy and routing rules.

messages.text: I have drafted a first version of the unified feedback taxonomy for T2 and captured it in A2. It currently has 14 top-level categories, grouped under themes like service quality, product, digital experience, billing, and safety, with examples for each. I also sketched initial routing rules into A5 so that each category maps to a primary owner team and an escalation path. Before we lock this down, I need your input: do these categories cover your real-world cases, and are the routing rules workable for the pilot?

I went through A2 and the categories look mostly aligned with what we see in help desk tickets. For T2, I suggest we split digital experience into two subcategories: access or login issues, and navigation or content issues. That will help us later when we analyse A6. On routing in A5, I noticed that some data privacy concerns are currently mapped to membership; I would route those to ICT or BI first so we can check compliance and T9 rules before responding.

From the membership side, the relationship and communication categories in A2 make sense, but I am not sure where to put feedback about membership pricing versus general billing. Right now I see a billing category, but members often mix comments about price with comments about benefits. Should we have a specific membership value category, or just tag those as billing plus membership relationship?

Looking at A2 from the insurance angle, the complaint and claims handling categories are good, but we should align them with our existing complaint codes for T7. I propose we add a subcategory under complaints for coverage disputes, since those have specific escalation rules. In A5, coverage disputes should route to insurance as primary, with a clear note that we cannot change terms, only clarify. I can prepare a mapping table for T7 that links each current code to the new taxonomy.

For cellar visits, I see product quality and safety in A2, which fits most of what visitors tell us. Sometimes they also comment on the tour schedule or group size. Would that go under service quality, or do we need a specific on-site experience subcategory so that T6 and A3 can point to it clearly?

On membership pricing versus general billing, I suggest we keep a single billing or pricing category but add a tag in A5 for membership-specific cases. That way T2 stays lean, and we can still filter membership-related billing feedback in A6. For comments about benefits, we can use the relationship or communication category plus the membership flag. I will update A2 with examples so it is clear for frontline staff.

For tour schedule and group size, I would place them under service quality with a specific on-site experience subcategory. That keeps T2 consistent while giving enough detail for cellar operations. I will add that subcategory to A2 and make sure A3 and T6 reference it so the checklist wording matches.

On routing for data privacy concerns, I agree they should not go to membership first. Maybe we can define a rule in A5 that any feedback tagged as privacy or data handling routes to ICT or BI as primary, with membership or insurance looped in only if the content is about their processes. That will also help us keep T9 aligned with actual practice.

I have started drafting the mapping table for T7. For each existing complaint code, I am assigning a primary category from A2 and a default routing rule in A5. Once that is ready, we can test it by reclassifying at least 10 historical complaints as required by T7. This should also surface any missing categories before we finalise T2.

Using a membership flag in A5 for billing or pricing feedback works for me. Could you add a couple of concrete examples in A2 for typical member questions, like renewal price increases or benefit changes, so the team can tag them consistently?

An on-site experience subcategory under service quality sounds good. If A3 and T6 can list examples like waiting time before the tour or clarity of safety instructions, that will help cellar staff choose the right tag when they hand over checklists into A5.

Agreed on routing for privacy-related feedback. I will update A2 to include a dedicated privacy and data handling category, and in A5 I will set the default owner to ICT or BI, depending on the channel. That will keep T9 and A7 consistent with how we actually handle these cases.

One more suggestion for T2: for help desk we often get feedback that mixes a technical issue with a compliment or complaint about the agent. Should we allow multiple tags per feedback item in A5, for example digital access plus service quality, so we do not lose nuance in A6?

Yes, I propose we allow one primary category plus up to two secondary tags in A5. That keeps reporting in A6 manageable while still capturing mixed feedback. I will document this rule in A2 under tagging guidelines for T2.

Once the mapping table for T7 is ready, I can run a quick test with 10 historical complaints and share the results here. If we see that any complaints do not fit well into the current A2 categories, we can adjust before we sign off on T2 and the routing rules.

Thanks for all the input. I have now updated A2 with the extra subcategories for digital access, navigation or content, on-site experience, and coverage disputes, plus the privacy category and membership examples. A5 has been adjusted so each category has a clear primary owner and escalation path, including the rule that privacy items go to ICT or BI first, and that we can use one primary and up to two secondary tags. Unless there are strong objections today, I will treat this taxonomy and the associated routing rules as final for the pilot and move T2 to done.
No objections from membership. The updated A2 examples and the membership flag in A5 should be enough for my team to tag feedback correctly.

No objections from insurance either. The coverage dispute subcategory and routing in A5 match our escalation rules. I will still complete the T7 reclassification test, but I am comfortable using this taxonomy in the pilot.
From the cellar side, the on-site experience and safety categories in A2 look clear. I can map the items in A3 and T6 to those without issues.

Given the confirmations from each team, I am marking the taxonomy in A2 and the routing rules in A5 as approved for the pilot. We will use this structure for tagging across all channels and for routing to membership, help desk, insurance, and cellar teams. Any changes during the pilot will be treated as controlled tweaks and captured for the final report.

next_steps.when: before first cellar tour in pilot

threads.thread_goal: Align on frontline scripts, checklists, and training approach.

messages.text: I have drafted the first version of the help desk intake script for T3 and added it into A4. It covers greeting, a short explanation of the feedback pilot, consent and data privacy notice aligned with A7, and a few key questions to capture structured feedback plus free text. I tried to keep it short enough to fit into normal calls. I would like your feedback on two points: 1) is the wording clear and friendly for members and visitors, and 2) does it work with your operational reality, especially for membership and cellar teams who will adapt parts of it for T4 and T6?

Thanks for sharing. I read through A4 and the tone feels appropriate. For membership, I might need a slightly shorter version for calls, maybe trimming one of the open questions so we do not extend call time too much. For T4, I can reuse your greeting and privacy lines, then add one or two membership-specific questions. Could you help me check that my version still matches A7 once I draft it?

For cellar tours, the full script in A4 is a bit long to use during the visit. I think we can use a shorter version at the end of the tour, combined with the checklist in A3 and T6. Maybe we can keep just a brief explanation of the pilot, a simple consent line, and one key question about the visit, then use the checklist to capture details. I will need help making sure the wording still respects A7.

From insurance, I see two uses for A4: one is when we proactively ask for feedback after a claim is closed, and the other is when a complaint naturally includes feedback. For the first, your script works with minor tweaks to mention claims. For the second, we might only use the consent and privacy parts, since the customer is already explaining their issue. I suggest we add a short note in A4 for insurance-specific adaptations so T7 and our complaint handling remain consistent.

I reviewed A4 and it aligns with A2 and A7 from a structure and compliance perspective. For T3, the key is that we always mention why we collect feedback, how it will be used, and that customers can decline. I like that you kept the questions focused on experience, not on personal data. For training under T10, we should highlight a couple of do and do not examples so staff feel comfortable using the script.

Happy to help with the membership version. If you share your draft for T4, I can cross-check it against A7 and make sure the consent and privacy lines stay accurate. We can also add a short note in A4 to show which parts are common across teams and which are membership-specific.

For the cellar version, I agree we should keep it very short. We can create a mini-script that just explains the pilot, asks for permission to note feedback on the A3 checklist, and reassures visitors about data use per A7. I can draft that and you can test it with a couple of tours before we finalise T6.

I will put together a shorter membership script today using your structure from A4 and send it over. For T4, I am thinking of one main question about overall satisfaction and one about how clear our communication was. If that works, we can keep it consistent with the help desk wording so customers hear similar phrases across channels.

A mini-script for tours sounds good. I can try it on two tours tomorrow and let you know if visitors seem comfortable with it. For the checklist in A3 and T6, I will also check that the questions are easy to ask in a group setting, not just one-on-one.

I can draft the insurance-specific note for A4, clarifying when we use the full script versus only the consent and privacy parts. That will help our team stay aligned with T7 and avoid asking customers to repeat themselves during complaints.

On training under T10, I propose we run short async sessions where each team reviews A4 and A3 or T6, then posts one example of how they would use the script in their context. That will surface any confusion early and we can adjust wording before the pilot starts.
Async examples work for membership. I can share a couple of sample call openings using the T4 script and A4 wording once we finalise them, and capture any questions from the team for T10.
I can record a short written example of how I would introduce the checklist from A3 at the end of a tour and share it for T10. That should help other cellar staff feel more confident using T6.

Based on your feedback, I have updated A4 with three variants: core help desk script for T3, a shorter membership version for T4, and a mini cellar version linked to A3 and T6. All share the same privacy and consent wording aligned with A7. I also added a short insurance note that 225681 will refine. Please take one more look and confirm if you are comfortable using these versions in the pilot.
The membership version in A4 looks good to me. I can use it as the base for T4 and train the team under T10 without major changes.

I tested the mini cellar script from A4 on two tours and it worked fine. Visitors understood the pilot and were ok with the checklist in A3. I am comfortable using this version for T6 during the pilot.

I have refined the insurance note in A4 and it now clearly states when we use the full script versus only the consent and privacy parts. This aligns with T7 and our complaint handling. I am ok using this in the pilot.

From a project perspective, the updated A4 and A3 look ready for pilot use. They are consistent with A2 and A7 and fit within our operational constraints. I suggest we formally adopt these scripts and the cellar checklist for the pilot and move ahead with T10 training.

next_steps.when: before first help desk shift in pilot

threads.thread_goal: Set up KPI tracking, data protection rules, and dashboard expectations.

messages.text: For the pilot KPIs and data handling, I have drafted a proposal in A6 and a first version of the data protection guideline in A7, linked to T5 and T9. The core KPIs I am suggesting are: total feedback volume by channel and category, resolution time from receipt to closure, share of feedback with follow-up action, and basic sentiment. On data protection, A7 defines who can access which fields in A5 and A6, and how long we retain identifiable data. Please review and let me know if these KPIs are sufficient for your teams and if the access rules are workable in practice.

From the help desk side, the proposed KPIs in A6 make sense. I would add one more: percentage of feedback items with missing or inconsistent tags, so we can quickly spot training needs. On A7 and T9, I like that access to free-text fields is limited to a smaller group, with frontline teams mainly seeing structured fields in A5. That should reduce privacy risk while still letting us act on issues.

For membership, the KPIs you listed cover most of what we need. It would be helpful if A6 can also show feedback volume specifically from members versus non-members, maybe using the membership flag in A5. On A7, I want to be sure that when we use T8 to communicate about the pilot, we can honestly say that only a limited group sees personal details. The current wording seems to say that, but I would appreciate a double-check.

From insurance, I would like A6 to include a breakdown of complaints versus general feedback, and within complaints, a view by the T7 categories like coverage disputes versus service issues. That will help us show stakeholders that we are not just counting complaints but also learning from them. On A7 and T9, the retention periods for complaint-related feedback should match our regulatory requirements; I can cross-check that and suggest any adjustments.

For the cellar, I mainly need a simple view of how many checklists from A3 we collected, what the main issues were, and if any safety-related feedback came up. If A6 can show a small section for cellar feedback, that will be enough. On A7, I want to confirm that paper checklists from T6 are stored securely and that we know how long to keep them before anonymising or discarding.

Good idea on tracking missing or inconsistent tags. I will add a data quality KPI to A6 and a small section in A7 explaining that we will use it only for training and process improvement, not for individual evaluation. That should help us keep T5 focused on learning.

On member versus non-member views, we can use the membership flag in A5 to create a dedicated slice in A6. I will also re-read A7 to ensure the wording matches what you want to say in T8 about limited access to personal details. If needed, we can tighten the language so it is fully accurate.

I can help double-check that the T8 message lines up with A7. Once you have a near-final draft of T8, send it over and I will verify that the statements about who can see what data are correct based on T9 and A7.

I have checked our regulatory retention rules and they require us to keep complaint records for a longer period than general feedback. I propose we reflect that in A7 and T9 by having two retention timelines: one for complaints as defined in T7, and one shorter one for general feedback. I can draft the exact wording if you agree.

On paper checklists, I can make sure they are stored in a locked cabinet and handed over weekly for entry into A5 and A6. We just need A7 and T9 to say how long we keep the original paper forms before shredding or anonymising.

I will incorporate the complaints versus general feedback breakdown into A6, using the T7 categories for coverage disputes and service issues. That will give us a clear view for the final report and A8. On retention, I support your proposal for two timelines; please go ahead and draft the wording for A7 and T9.

One more point on access rules: for training and quality checks, it would help if a small group of supervisors in each team could see more detail in A5 and A6, while most frontline staff only see what they need to act. A7 already hints at this, but we might want to list roles explicitly in T9 so there is no confusion.

Agreed. I will update T9 and A7 to list role-based access: BI and ICT with full access for analysis and troubleshooting, a small set of supervisors in each team with extended access, and frontline staff with limited fields needed to respond. That will also make it easier to explain in T8 and training under T10.

On KPIs, could we also see a simple trend in A6 for member satisfaction over the 30 days, even if it is just a basic positive or negative indicator? That would help us communicate early wins to stakeholders.
We can add a simple sentiment trend for members in A6, based on the sentiment field and the membership flag in A5. It will not be a full survey score, but it will show direction over the 30 days.

I have drafted the two-tier retention wording and added it to A7 and T9: complaints data retained for the regulatory period, general feedback for a shorter period, with anonymisation after that. Please review to confirm it matches your expectations.

I have now incorporated all the suggestions into A6 and A7: added data quality and member sentiment KPIs, complaint breakdown by T7 categories, a dedicated cellar section, and role-based access with two retention timelines. Unless there are objections, I propose we adopt these KPIs as the core set for the pilot and approve the data protection and access rules so we can start T5 and T11 on time.
No objections from help desk. The KPIs and access rules in A6 and A7 are clear and workable.
Membership is ok with the KPI set and the data rules as described in A7. The member versus non-member split in A6 will be very useful.
Insurance is aligned as well. The complaint breakdown and retention rules in A7 and T9 meet our needs.
From the cellar side, the simple section in A6 and the storage rules in A7 are fine. I can follow them without issues.

Thanks all. With your confirmations, we will use this KPI set in A6 as the core metrics for the pilot and adopt the data protection and access rules in A7 and T9. I will proceed to finalise T5 and ensure the dashboard is ready for the first weekly snapshot.

threads.thread_goal: Review pilot results and agree on next steps and roadmap.

messages.text: We have reached the end of the 30-day pilot, and I have compiled the preliminary results in A8 based on data from A6 and logs in A5, aligned with T11 and T12. High level: we captured more feedback than expected across all channels, routing accuracy improved over the month, and resolution times decreased slightly. We also identified a few process gaps and system limitations. I would like each of you to share your perspective: what worked well, what was painful, and what you would change if we extend or scale this beyond the pilot.

From the help desk side, the intake script in A4 and the taxonomy in A2 worked well once agents got used to them. Tagging quality improved over the month, as shown in the data quality KPI in A6. The main pain point was manual entry into A5 when systems did not support tags directly. If we scale, I would like to explore light configuration changes or automation to reduce double work, while keeping T9 and A7 rules intact.

For membership, the short script from A4 and the member flag in A5 helped us capture more structured feedback than before. Members reacted positively to being asked. The challenge was fitting the extra questions into already busy calls, especially at peak times. If we continue, I would like to adjust T4 slightly so we only ask the full set on certain interactions, and maybe use email follow-ups for others.

On the insurance side, the mapping in T7 and the routing rules in A5 worked well. We were able to reclassify historical complaints and see clear patterns in A6, especially for coverage disputes versus service issues. The main friction was the time needed to re-tag older cases; for a scaled rollout, I would focus on new complaints only and selectively reclassify older ones where needed for analysis.

For the cellar, the checklist in A3 and the mini-script from A4 were easy enough to use, and visitors gave useful comments about tours and safety. The main issue was remembering to fill in A3 during very busy days. If we extend the approach, I would like to keep using T6 but maybe limit it to certain tour types or time slots so it does not interfere with operations.

On manual entry into A5, I agree that is not sustainable at larger scale. In A8 I have noted a recommendation to explore simple configuration changes or shared forms that feed directly into A6, within our existing tools and budget constraints. We will need IT operations to validate what is feasible, but the pilot data from T11 gives us a strong case.
That sounds good. I can help specify the minimum data fields we need in any configured solution, based on what worked in A5 and A6 during the pilot, so we do not overcomplicate things.

On adjusting T4, I would welcome guidance on which interactions to prioritise for the full question set. Maybe we can use the patterns in A6 to see where member feedback had the most impact and focus there if we extend the pilot.

I agree that for a broader rollout we should focus on new complaints. The T7 mapping is now stable, and A6 already gives us a good baseline from the pilot. We can always run targeted reclassification later if we need deeper historical analysis.

If we limit T6 to certain tour types, I suggest we pick the ones with the highest visitor volume, so we still get enough data for A6 without overloading staff. The pilot numbers in A8 should help us choose.

Using A6 to identify which membership interactions generate the most actionable feedback is a good idea. In A8 I have already flagged renewals and benefit change discussions as high-yield moments. For a scaled approach, we can recommend using the full T4 script there and a lighter touch elsewhere.

From a privacy and data handling perspective, A7 and T9 held up well during the pilot. We had a couple of edge cases where customers asked to see or delete their feedback, and we were able to respond using the documented rules. If we scale, we might want to add a short internal FAQ to A7 with these scenarios.

Looking at the KPIs in A6, I see clear value in continuing: we have better visibility into complaint drivers and can show improvements in resolution time. The incremental effort for insurance is manageable now that T7 is in place. My view is that we should extend and gradually scale, starting with the current channels and then adding more automation as suggested in A8.

From the cellar perspective, I would like to continue using A3 and T6, but with a slightly reduced frequency to avoid overload on peak days. The feedback we collected was useful for improving tours and safety briefings, and the effort felt reasonable most of the time.

For membership, I also see value in continuing, especially because the member sentiment trend in A6 helped us spot issues early. I would support extending the approach, with some adjustments to T4 and T10 to better fit our workload.
Help desk is also in favour of continuing, provided we can reduce manual steps over time. The pilot showed that structured feedback and routing via A5 really helped us spot recurring issues faster.

Based on your feedback and the results in A8, my recommendation is to extend the current setup and gradually scale it, rather than stopping or jumping straight to a full rollout. Concretely, we would keep the same channels and taxonomy, refine scripts and checklists where needed, and work with IT to reduce manual logging. We would also continue tracking KPIs in A6 and update A7 or T9 if new privacy scenarios appear. Unless there are strong objections, I will frame the final T12 report around this extend-and-scale recommendation.
I support the extend-and-scale approach. It balances the benefits we saw in A6 with the effort required, and it gives us room to improve tooling over time.
I am also ok with extending, as long as we keep the flexibility on when to use T6 in the cellar. The improvements to tours are worth it.
Membership is aligned with extending and gradually scaling, with the adjustments we discussed for T4 and T10.
Help desk agrees with the recommendation. Continuing will let us build on the tagging and routing habits we developed during T11.

Thanks for confirming. I will finalise A8 and T12 with the decision to extend and gradually scale the feedback process, including a roadmap for tooling improvements, script refinements, and ongoing KPI tracking. I will also summarise key lessons learned from T11 so leadership can see the impact clearly.
